summary: This joint resolution uses the Congressional Review Act to disapprove and cancel a Bureau of Land Management rule from April 25, 2022, regarding the National Petroleum Reserve in Alaska. By nullifying the 2022 plan, which had closed about 48 percent of the reserve to oil and gas leasing to protect surface resources and wildlife, the resolution reverts management back to the 2020 plan and reopens portions of the reserve for oil and gas leasing.

affected_groups.effect: Lose protections provided under the 2022 plan that were established to provide subsistence for communities.
Lose protections established under the 2022 plan.
Portions of the approximately 23-million-acre reserve are reopened for oil and gas leasing.

key_provisions: Expresses congressional disapproval of the Bureau of Land Management rule titled National Petroleum Reserve in Alaska Integrated Activity Plan Record of Decision, issued on April 25, 2022.
Declares that the disapproved rule shall have no force or effect.
Removes the protections and closures put in place by the 2022 plan that closed approximately 48% of the reserve to oil and gas leasing.
Reverts management of the National Petroleum Reserve in Alaska to the 2020 plan.
Reopens portions of the National Petroleum Reserve for oil and gas leasing.

summary_detail.plain_summary: This joint resolution uses the Congressional Review Act to disapprove and cancel a Bureau of Land Management rule from April 25, 2022, regarding the National Petroleum Reserve in Alaska. By nullifying the 2022 plan, which had closed about 48 percent of the reserve to oil and gas leasing to protect surface resources and wildlife, the resolution reverts management back to the 2020 plan and reopens portions of the reserve for oil and gas leasing.
summary_detail.significance: The joint resolution changes federal land and energy policy by overturning an executive branch administrative rule for a 23-million-acre reserve, shifting management back to an older framework that allows more access for oil and gas leasing while removing specific wildlife and subsistence protections.
